vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: gws-gmail-reply
Version: 1.0.10

The skill is a standard wrapper for the 'gws' CLI tool to handle Gmail replies. It provides expected functionality such as message threading, attachments, and HTML support without any signs of malicious intent, data exfiltration, or prompt injection in SKILL.md.

llm.summary: The skill is an instruction-only wrapper that delegates reply actions to a local 'gws' CLI and is internally consistent, but it defers authentication and security rules to a separate shared SKILL.md that is not included so you should inspect that file and the installed gws binary before using it.

dimensions.detail: The skill name/description map cleanly to the declared requirement: the 'gws' binary. No unrelated binaries, credentials, or config paths are requested in this bundle.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: All runtime instructions are limited to invoking the gws CLI to construct and send replies. However the SKILL.md explicitly refers to ../gws-shared/SKILL.md for auth, global flags, and security rules; that external file is not included here, so the effective auth behavior and any additional runtime instructions are unknown and must be reviewed in gws-shared.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: Instruction-only skill with no install spec and no code files — nothing is written to disk by this bundle itself. The only runtime dependency is that a trusted 'gws' binary exist on PATH.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill declares no required environment variables. Authentication is delegated to gws-shared, which likely manages tokens/credentials; because that file is missing from this bundle, you should check gws-shared to see what secrets or files are needed and where they are stored.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill does not request permanent presence (always:false) and does not claim to modify other skills or system-wide agent settings. Autonomous invocation is allowed (platform default) and is normal for this type of skill.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill itself is a thin wrapper around a local 'gws' CLI and looks coherent for replying to Gmail messages. Before installing: (1) Verify the 'gws' binary on your machine is the legitimate, up-to-date tool you expect (check vendor, checksum, and install source). (2) Locate and review ../gws-shared/SKILL.md (or run the suggested gws generate-skills only after reviewing what it will create) to understand authentication flows, where tokens/credentials are stored, and any global security rules. (3) Prefer testing with --dry-run and a non-production account first. (4) Do not grant or place OAuth tokens or credentials into locations you haven't reviewed; confirm attachments and file paths are provided by you at runtime rather than being automatically discovered by the tool.
